BCUs_Applied_to_Bio_Oil_Transport_Proces.anomaly_finding: **MATERIAL ISSUE.** BCU value 5.582 t is 4.453 t higher than 2-188's transport process emissions (1.129 t = 0.187 + 0.867 + 0.075). Sister batches' BCUs match transport process exactly: 2-186=1.621 t (verified by direct Certify read), 2-187=1.612 t (verified), 2-189=1.617 t (verified, 268+1242+107). The excess 4.453 t flows into Net CDR as positive credit (since Net = Seq + BCU − Activities − Uncertainty). Inflates 2-188's Net from a sister-pattern-expected ~21.05 t to actual 25.50 t, a ~17% over-credit. BCU source file (Charm-A4-2024-10-24-63-1976.pdf) is DIFFERENT from sister 2-189's source (Charm-A3-2024-10-24-64-1976.pdf) — possibly a different certificate batch with a different carbon-credit value baked in. Either: (a) Charm intentionally over-allocated BCU to this last-offload removal, in which case the rationale needs documentation visible to the verifier; or (b) the wrong certificate or value was linked. Worth surfacing to Garrett to verify whether 5,581.52 kgCO2e is the correct allocation for THIS removal.
